question.prompt:
In rectangle \(ABCD,\) points \(F\) and \(G\) lie on \(\overline{AB}\) so that \(AF = FG = GB\) and \(E\) is the midpoint of \(\overline{DC}.\) Also, \(\overline{AC}\) intersects \(\overline{EF}\) at \(H\) and \(\overline{EG}\) at \(J.\) The area of rectangle \(ABCD\) is \(70.\) Find the area of triangle \(EHJ.\)

[Figure 1](figures/2001_AMC_12_Q22_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Because \(H\) and \(J\) lie on diagonal \(AC\), triangles \(EHJ\) and \(EAC\) have the same altitude to that diagonal. Their areas are therefore in the ratio \(HJ:AC\). We can find this length ratio using the parallel top and bottom sides of the rectangle.

Since \(AF\parallel EC\), triangles \(AFH\) and \(CEH\) are similar: their angles at \(H\) are vertical angles, and another pair comes from the parallel sides. Corresponding sides give
\[
\frac{AH}{HC}=\frac{AF}{EC}
=\frac{AB/3}{AB/2}=\frac23.
\]
Thus \(AH\) is two of the five equal ratio parts of \(AC\), so
\[
\frac{AH}{AC}=\frac25.
\]
Similarly, triangles \(AGJ\) and \(CEJ\) are similar, giving
\[
\frac{AJ}{JC}=\frac{AG}{EC}
=\frac{2AB/3}{AB/2}=\frac43,
\qquad
\frac{AJ}{AC}=\frac47.
\]
Since \(2/5<4/7\), the order on the diagonal is \(A,H,J,C\). Hence
\[
\frac{HJ}{AC}=\frac47-\frac25=\frac6{35}.
\]
Write \([XYZ]\) for the area of triangle \(XYZ\). Triangle \(EAC\) has base \(EC=AB/2\) and height \(AD\), so
\[
[EAC]=\frac12\cdot\frac{AB}{2}\cdot AD
=\frac{70}{4}.
\]
Using the common altitude to \(AC\), we obtain
\[
[EHJ]=\frac{HJ}{AC}[EAC]
=\frac6{35}\cdot\frac{70}{4}
=\boxed3.
\]
The answer is \(\mathrm{C}\).
solutions.title: Find diagonal fractions using similar triangles

solutions.explanation:
Coordinates let us find the heights of \(H\) and \(J\) while keeping the rectangle's side lengths unknown. Let \(AB=w>0\) and \(AD=h>0\), so \(wh=70\). Place
\[
A=(0,0),\quad B=(w,0),\quad
C=(w,h),\quad D=(0,h).
\]
The given divisions then give
\[
F=(w/3,0),\quad G=(2w/3,0),\quad E=(w/2,h).
\]
The diagonal \(AC\) has equation \(y=(h/w)x\). Using the two known endpoints of each line, we obtain
\[
EF:\quad y=\frac{6h}{w}x-2h,
\qquad
EG:\quad y=-\frac{6h}{w}x+4h.
\]
At \(H\), the equations of \(AC\) and \(EF\) agree, so
\[
\frac hw x=\frac{6h}{w}x-2h,
\]
which gives \(x=2w/5\) and \(y=2h/5\). At \(J\),
\[
\frac hw x=-\frac{6h}{w}x+4h,
\]
which gives \(x=4w/7\) and \(y=4h/7\). The divisions are valid because \(w,h>0\).

Now use the horizontal segment \(EC\), of length \(w/2\), as a common base. The heights from \(H\) and \(J\) to its line are respectively \(3h/5\) and \(3h/7\). Thus, writing brackets for triangle areas,
\[
[EHC]=\frac12\cdot\frac w2\cdot\frac{3h}{5}
=\frac{3wh}{20},
\]
\[
[EJC]=\frac12\cdot\frac w2\cdot\frac{3h}{7}
=\frac{3wh}{28}.
\]
The intersection coordinates show the order \(A,H,J,C\), so segment \(EJ\) divides triangle \(EHC\) into triangles \(EHJ\) and \(EJC\). Therefore
\[
[EHJ]=\frac{3wh}{20}-\frac{3wh}{28}
=\frac{3wh}{70}
=\boxed3.
\]
The answer is \(\mathrm{C}\).
solutions.title: Find the intersection heights with coordinates
